title: How to use VS Code for data analysts on mac: a guide to better workflows
metaTitle: VS Code for data analysts on Mac: Setup, Shortcuts, and Tips for 2026
description: Learn how to optimize VS Code for data analysts on Mac. Master shortcuts, extensions, and environment setup to clean data and run Python faster.
targetKeyword: vs code for data analysts on mac
intro: You can turn VS Code into a powerhouse for data analysis on Mac by focusing on the right extensions and terminal settings. Many analysts struggle with setup, but once you configure your environment, you gain speed in cleaning data and running scripts. This guide shows you how to bridge the gap between simple text editing and professional data science workflows on macOS.
tldr: Use File > Open Folder to ensure IntelliSense works across your entire project.
Install the Python and Pylance extensions to enable proper code execution.
Master the Command Palette with Cmd + Shift + P to access all settings.
Use the integrated terminal with Control + Backtick to run SQL or Python scripts.
Use Lazur to quickly ask about settings or find hidden menu options without leaving your flow.

blocks.text: Setting up your Mac for data analysis

Data analysis requires a stable environment. Start by downloading the latest stable build from the official website. Once installed, avoid opening single files. Always use File > Open Folder. This allows VS Code to index your project, which makes autocomplete and search much faster. Without this, you lose the benefits of IntelliSense across your data files.

VS Code is an editor, not a compiler. You must install extensions to get real work done. The Python extension is mandatory for data science. It provides support for Jupyter notebooks, which are standard for exploration. Also, consider adding SQL tools to interact with your databases directly from the editor.

items: Python: Essential for data manipulation and scripting.
Jupyter: Allows you to run notebooks inside VS Code.
SQL Server or PostgreSQL: Helps you query databases without switching apps.
Prettier: Keeps your code clean and readable.

blocks.text: Speed comes from keeping your hands on the keyboard. Learning the core shortcuts saves you hours of menu hunting. Use Cmd + Shift + P to open the Command Palette. This is your gateway to every feature in the app. Use Cmd + P for quick file navigation. When working with large datasets, use Cmd + Shift + F to search for variables across every file in your folder.

You will spend a lot of time in the terminal. Use Control + Backtick to toggle the integrated terminal. You can run your scripts or check database connections here. If you need to change your default shell, you can do so in the settings. This ensures you are using your preferred environment, like Zsh or Bash, every time you open the terminal.

Many analysts get frustrated when they cannot find their files. If you open a file in Preview Mode, the name appears in italics. If you click another file, the first one disappears. Double-click the tab to pin it. If your interface looks wrong, go to View > Appearance > Reset View Locations to bring back your sidebar and terminal.
Using Lazur to stay in the zone

When you are deep in data cleaning, you do not want to stop to look up a setting. Hold Option + Command and ask Lazur where a specific setting is. It will circle the button or menu item on your screen. You can also ask it how to format a document or set a breakpoint. It helps you keep your focus on the data.

faq.question: Is VS Code free to use on Mac?
faq.answer: Yes, VS Code is free and open source. You can download it directly from the official website.

faq.question: Can I run Jupyter notebooks in VS Code?
faq.answer: Yes, once you install the Python extension, you can open and run .ipynb files directly in the editor.

faq.question: How do I search for text across all files?
faq.answer: Use the shortcut Cmd + Shift + F to open the global search sidebar.
